newsitem.title: PERU: Shell starts drilling in Peru's Camisea.
newsitem.headline: Shell starts drilling in Peru's Camisea.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell started drilling Tuesday to appraise the reserves in Peru's huge Camisea oil condensate and gas fields, the company said.
Shell began drilling a well in the Cashiriari field, one of two large reserves in the Camisea area, Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. said in a statement.
Oil giants Shell and Mobil signed a contract with the government last year that gives them the rights for two years to appraise Camisea's reserves with a view to developing them.
Shell estimates it will invest over $100 million in this two-year period.

"Comencement of drilling operations some 10 months after signing the Camisea licence agreement and 10 years after their discovery represents a major milestone in the realization of the project," said the project's general manager Alan Hunt.
Shell has said data will be collected from the well for 100 days before the firm moves on to drill wells in the San Martin field and a second in Cashiriari.

These two fields and the smaller Mipaya make up the Camisea reserves, situated 310 miles (500 km) east of Lima and estimated to hold 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids.

If the oil consortium, in which Shell is the operating partner with a 57.5 percent share, exploits the reserves, the project will last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at up to an estimated $3.0 billion.
The fields hold six times the rest of the country's reserves, according to the government, which estimates it will receive $6 billion in tax revenue from the project during the first 30 years.
